messages:
Alice H: :rotating_light: paging SRE — alerts showing sustained queue growth on gpu-pool-4, high throttling. requests/sec stayed steady but backlog increased. seeing 503s to some customers.
IncidentBot: Incident created: INC-2061234567 — GPU pool backlog + autoscale failed. Severity: P1. Pager notified: Ben (oncall). Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2061234567
Ben (oncall): On it. grabbing metrics now. first check — is this a spike or sustained?
SRE Lead: early hypothesis: continuous batching params were rolled out to dedicated pools last night (continuous_batching.v2). suspect batch formation + prefix_cache miss storm reduced throughput, autoscaler couldn't keep up.
Eng Runtime: confirming — rollout started at 02:14UTC. new batching window lowered flush threshold (max_latency_ms -> 12ms) and prefix_cache.ttl was shortened from 600s to 60s in the same PR (deploy/4572).
Ben (oncall): Metrics:
```
gpu-pool-4 queue_depth: 12k -> 38k
per_gpu_utilization: 98%
avg_latency(p50/p95): 85ms / 420ms
autoscaler_add_events: 0 (at cap)
scale_limit: 12 gpus
```
Ben (oncall): autoscaler hit configured scale_limit (12) and then started throttling requests. requests were queued and continuous batching made larger batches but kernel scheduling got worse due to cache churn.
Infra Ops: Confirmed no underlying host failures. capacity exhausted by sustained load + reduced effective throughput.
Customer Success: Received 2 customer reports with higher error rates for inference. emails coming in.
Alice H: Immediate mitigation ideas? rollback, increase scale_limit, emergency bypass of continuous batching for gpu-pool-4.
Eng Runtime: Quickest safe path: toggle continuous_batching back to previous profile (continuous_batching.v1) for the affected pool and restore prefix_cache.ttl to 600s. That can be done via feature-flag and rollout rollback in console. PR/4572 rollback prepared (hotfix/4572-revert).
SRE Lead: Also consider temporary model-fallback routing to cpu-backend for low-priority/non-SLA customers to relieve GPU. Could route by customer tier.
Ben (oncall): Doing rollback now. Command I ran: `kubectl set env deploy/rt-serving CONT_BATCH_PROFILE=continuous_batching.v1 -n redwood-gpu-pool-4`
Ben (oncall): Patching prefix cache: `curl -XPOST https://config.redwood.internal/pools/gpu-pool-4/cache -d '{"prefix_cache.ttl":600}'`
Ben (oncall): Rolling out. Will watch queue.
(5m later)
Ben (oncall): Rollback accepted, configs applied. queue depth dropping: 38k -> 9k. autoscaler still at cap but throughput per GPU improving. p95 latency down to 210ms.
Eng Runtime: neat — that aligns. continuous_batching.v2's aggressive flush/packing plus shorter prefix ttl caused excessive cache misses and recompute. That increased per-token GPU work and reduced throughput.
SRE Lead: Next steps: keep rollback on gpu-pool-4. revert PR/4572 fully and run a canary with smaller traffic slice, add a safety guard in the rollout to prevent simultaneous batching+cache param changes.
Infra Ops: We should also increase autoscaler hard limit to 18 gpus for emergency capacity while we validate the rollback. Raising limit now requires approval but we can flip emergency flag for scheduled pools.
Ben (oncall): I enabled emergency_scale_override=18 for gpu-pool-4 temporarily. monitoring.
Customer Success: Notifying affected customers: drafting status update. Will include ETA and mitigation details.
Alice H: Good. Log entry for postmortem: record combined config change + rollout without staggered risk check, autoscaler cap too tight for worst-case recompute. Also capture that alert runbook needs a quick config check action.
Eng Runtime: Adding guard: disallow simultaneous changes to continuous_batching.* and prefix_cache.* in a single deploy. Also adding a perf-test that simulates prefix_cache miss storms.
(10m later)
Ben (oncall): Queue now at 2.1k, p95 latency 110ms, error rate returning to baseline. Autoscale now at 14 GPUs (some manual scale). Setting incident status to "mitigated" pending postmortem.
IncidentBot: Incident INC-2061234567 status changed to MITIGATED by Ben (oncall).
SRE Lead: Assigning postmortem owners: Eng Runtime + SRE Lead. Draft due EOD tomorrow.
Customer Success: Sent status update to affected customers, included rollback and ETA. No major data loss, degraded availability only.
Alice H: Thanks team. follow-ups: 1) revert PR/4572, 2) add rollout guard, 3) adjust runbook, 4) consider autoscaler safety buffer. I'll create tasks. :thumbsup:
Ben (oncall): leaving detailed timeline & commands in incident ticket. toggling notifications back to normal.
Eng Runtime: small note for postmortem — add an A/B perf benchmark between v1 and v2 under high prefix-miss conditions.
Customer Success: closing customer comms loop unless new reports surface.
Alice H: closing thread here. good job. :clap:
